reason: This text (Exodus 11-12, the narrative of the tenth plague and the Exodus) describes God protecting and liberating the Israelites from Egypt. God kills the Egyptian firstborn while explicitly sparing the Israelite firstborn ('and against all the children of Israel not a dog will move his tongue... that you may know that the Lord makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel'). The Hebrews are shown receiving divine favor, not facing a threat of death. Critically, the text contains no condition or threat that Yahweh will kill the Hebrews if they don't worship properly—it is rather a narrative of deliverance where God saves Israel regardless.
